about: Everyday Indian breakfasts and main courses. Nutrition is approximate, for one typical home-cooked serving; it changes with recipe, oil and portion.

meals.name: Masala Dosa
highlights: The fermented rice and urad dal batter is easy to digest.
The potato filling adds potassium and vitamin B6.

meals.name: Idli with Sambar
highlights: Steamed, so it's low in fat.
Sambar's toor dal and vegetables add protein and fibre.

meals.name: Medu Vada
highlights: Urad dal gives it a good amount of plant protein.
Deep fried, so best as an occasional treat.

meals.name: Rava Upma
highlights: Quick to make and filling.
Add peas and carrots for extra fibre and vitamin A.

meals.name: Kanda Poha
highlights: Flattened rice is light and quick to cook.
A squeeze of lemon adds vitamin C, which helps the body absorb iron.

meals.name: Aloo Paratha
highlights: Whole-wheat flour adds fibre.
Serve with curd for protein and calcium.

meals.name: Methi Thepla
highlights: Fenugreek leaves add iron and vitamin K.
Keeps well, so it's good for travel and lunch boxes.

meals.name: Besan Chilla
highlights: Chickpea flour is high in plant protein and folate.
A quick high-protein breakfast.

meals.name: Pesarattu
highlights: Whole green moong is rich in protein, fibre and folate.
No fermenting needed; soak the moong overnight.

meals.name: Onion Uttapam
highlights: Made from the same fermented batter as dosa.
Top with tomatoes and capsicum for more vitamins.

meals.name: Ven Pongal
highlights: Rice and moong dal together give a complete protein.
Black pepper and cumin are traditional for digestion.

meals.name: Puri Bhaji
highlights: A festive favourite.
Deep fried, so best as an occasional treat.

meals.name: Masala Omelette
highlights: Eggs give complete protein, vitamin B12 and choline.
Ready in 10 minutes.

meals.name: Egg Bhurji
highlights: Indian-style scrambled eggs with onion and tomato.
Good with toast or rotis.

meals.name: Sabudana Khichdi
highlights: Popular on fasting days.
Peanuts add protein and healthy fats; it's mostly quick energy.

meals.name: Appam with Vegetable Stew
highlights: Coconut milk makes the stew creamy.
Carrots and beans add vitamin A and fibre.

meals.name: Paneer Paratha
highlights: Paneer adds protein and calcium.
Filling enough for a late breakfast.

meals.name: Khaman Dhokla
highlights: Steamed chickpea-flour cake: light and spongy.
Low in fat for a savoury snack.

meals.name: Semiya Upma
highlights: Vermicelli cooks in minutes.
Add vegetables to make it more filling.

meals.name: Ragi Dosa
highlights: Finger millet (ragi) is one of the richest plant sources of calcium.
Instant: no fermenting needed.

meals.name: Dal Tadka
highlights: Lentils are a staple source of plant protein and folate.
Pair with rice or rotis for a complete protein.

meals.name: Dal Makhani
highlights: Whole urad and rajma make it high in fibre.
Rich with butter and cream: a weekend dish.

meals.name: Rajma
highlights: Kidney beans are very high in fibre and plant protein.
Classic with steamed rice.

meals.name: Chana Masala
highlights: Chickpeas are rich in fibre, protein and folate.
Keeps you full for a long time.

meals.name: Palak Paneer
highlights: Spinach adds vitamins A and K; paneer adds protein and calcium.
Pair with lemon or tomatoes to help absorb the spinach's iron.

meals.name: Matar Paneer
highlights: Peas add fibre and a little extra protein.
A good everyday paneer curry.

meals.name: Paneer Butter Masala
highlights: Paneer is a good vegetarian source of protein and calcium.
Rich with butter and cream: a treat dish.

meals.name: Chicken Curry
highlights: Chicken is a lean, complete protein.
Home style: onion and tomato gravy.

meals.name: Butter Chicken
highlights: High in protein.
Rich with butter and cream: a weekend dish.

meals.name: Tandoori Chicken
highlights: Grilled or baked rather than fried.
One of the highest-protein dishes here.

meals.name: Chicken Biryani
highlights: A full meal in one pot.
Serve with raita for calcium and probiotics.

meals.name: Vegetable Biryani
highlights: Mixed vegetables add fibre and vitamins.
Add paneer or chickpeas for more protein.

meals.name: Egg Curry
highlights: Eggs give complete protein and vitamin B12.
A quick curry for busy evenings.

meals.name: Kerala Fish Curry
highlights: Fish adds omega-3 fats, especially oily fish like mackerel or sardines.
Kodampuli (gamboge) gives the classic tang.

meals.name: Mutton Rogan Josh
highlights: Red meat is rich in easily absorbed iron, zinc and B12.
Slow cooked until tender.

meals.name: Sambar Rice
highlights: Dal and vegetables in one comforting bowl.
Add a spoon of ghee if you like it richer.

meals.name: Rasam Rice
highlights: Light and soothing, often made when someone's under the weather.
Tomato and tamarind give it a tangy, peppery broth.

meals.name: Curd Rice
highlights: Curd has live cultures and calcium.
Cooling on hot days and gentle on the stomach.

meals.name: Lemon Rice
highlights: A good way to use leftover rice.
Peanuts add crunch and some protein.

meals.name: Moong Dal Khichdi
highlights: Rice and dal together give a complete protein.
Easy to digest; a go-to when someone's unwell.

meals.name: Kadhi Pakora
highlights: Curd and besan make a tangy, comforting curry.
Pakoras are fried, so it's on the richer side.

meals.name: Aloo Gobi
highlights: Cauliflower is a good source of vitamin C.
A simple dry sabzi for rotis.

meals.name: Bhindi Masala
highlights: Okra is rich in fibre and vitamin K.
Dry the okra well before cutting so it doesn't go slimy.

meals.name: Baingan Bharta
highlights: Roasting the brinjal gives it a smoky flavour.
Low in calories and high in fibre.

meals.name: Avial
highlights: Many vegetables in one dish.
Coconut and curd make it creamy.

meals.name: Mixed Vegetable Curry
highlights: A way to use whatever vegetables are in the fridge.
Light enough for weeknights.

meals.name: Chole Bhature
highlights: Chickpeas bring protein and fibre.
Fried bhaturas make it heavy: a weekend special.

meals.name: Pav Bhaji
highlights: The bhaji is packed with mashed vegetables.
Go easy on the butter to keep it lighter.

meals.name: Plain Dosa with Coconut Chutney
highlights: The everyday dosa: fermented rice and urad dal.
Coconut chutney with roasted chana dal adds a little protein.

meals.name: Rava Dosa
highlights: Crisp and lacy, with no fermenting needed.
Pour the thin batter from a height for the classic holes.

meals.name: Mysore Masala Dosa
highlights: Spread with a spicy red garlic chutney before the potato filling.
Richer than masala dosa, often finished with butter.

meals.name: Set Dosa with Sagu
highlights: Soft, thick and spongy, cooked on one side only.
Traditionally served with a vegetable sagu.

meals.name: Neer Dosa
highlights: Thin, soft rice crepes with no fermenting.
Very light; good with chicken curry or coconut chutney.

meals.name: Adai
highlights: Several dals make it one of the highest-protein South Indian breakfasts.
Traditionally eaten with avial or jaggery.

meals.name: Puttu with Kadala Curry
highlights: Steamed layers of rice flour and coconut with a black chickpea curry.
Black chickpeas add a lot of fibre and plant protein.

meals.name: Idiyappam with Vegetable Kurma
highlights: Steamed string hoppers are light and low in fat.
The coconut kurma makes it a filling meal.

meals.name: Kuzhi Paniyaram
highlights: A good use of leftover dosa batter.
Cooked in a paniyaram pan with very little oil.

meals.name: Akki Roti
highlights: Rice-flour flatbread patted out by hand.
Dill and carrot add flavour and vitamins.

meals.name: Rava Idli
highlights: Instant idli made with semolina and curd: no fermenting.
Said to have been created at Bengaluru's MTR during wartime rice shortages.

meals.name: Podi Idli
highlights: Mini idlis tossed in spicy lentil powder and ghee.
Good for lunch boxes and travel.

meals.name: Godhuma Dosa
highlights: Instant whole-wheat dosa for busy mornings.
Whole wheat adds fibre.

meals.name: Kanchipuram Idli
highlights: Temple-style spiced idli steamed in cups or leaves.
Pepper, cumin and dry ginger give it a warm flavour.

meals.name: Bisi Bele Bath
highlights: Rice, dal and vegetables in one spiced pot.
Served with boondi or potato chips in Karnataka.

meals.name: Vatha Kuzhambu with Rice
meals.serving: ½ cup kuzhambu with 1 cup rice
highlights: A tangy tamarind gravy that keeps for days.
Sun-dried turkey berries are traditional; shallots work too.

meals.name: Mor Kuzhambu with Rice
highlights: Curd simmered with a coconut paste: mild and comforting.
Ash gourd or okra are the usual vegetables.

meals.name: Poricha Kootu
highlights: Vegetables cooked with moong dal and a pepper-coconut paste.
Mild, so it's good for kids.

meals.name: Cabbage Thoran
highlights: Finely chopped cabbage stir-fried with fresh coconut.
Cabbage is a good source of vitamins C and K.

meals.name: Beans Poriyal
highlights: A quick dry stir-fry for rice and sambar.
Works with carrots, beetroot or cabbage too.

meals.name: Keerai Masiyal
highlights: Mashed greens with moong dal, eaten with rice and ghee.
Leafy greens bring vitamins A and K and folate.

meals.name: Andhra Tomato Pappu
highlights: Andhra's everyday dal, tangy with tomato.
Eaten with hot rice, ghee and pickle.

meals.name: Puliyogare
highlights: Tamarind rice that keeps well, so it's a travel favourite.
Peanuts add crunch and some protein.

meals.name: Coconut Rice
highlights: Leftover rice tossed with fresh coconut.
Mild and kid-friendly.

meals.name: Tomato Rice
highlights: One-pot rice for lunch boxes.
Serve with raita or a boiled egg for more protein.

meals.name: Chettinad Chicken Curry
highlights: Freshly roasted spices with plenty of black pepper.
One of Tamil Nadu's best-known curries.

meals.name: Gongura Mutton
highlights: Sour gongura leaves are Andhra's signature flavour.
Red meat gives easily absorbed iron and B12.

meals.name: Chemmeen Curry
highlights: Prawns in a tangy coconut gravy.
Prawns are high in protein and low in fat.

meals.name: Meen Varuval
highlights: Spice-marinated, shallow-fried fish.
Oily fish like seer or mackerel add omega-3 fats.

meals.name: Kerala Egg Roast
highlights: Boiled eggs in a slow-cooked onion masala.
Classic with appam, parotta or rice.

meals.name: Ragi Mudde with Saaru
highlights: Finger millet balls, eaten with a thin dal saaru.
Ragi is very high in calcium and keeps you full for a long time.

meals.name: Egg Kothu Parotta
highlights: Shredded parotta stir-fried with egg and spicy salna.
Street-food style and filling; best as a treat.
